notes: Added 60 original source-informed questions based on themes found across the uploaded Green Empire, VSU, UPLB/ACAP, and DOSCST reviewer collections.
10 new questions per ALE subject; emphasis on enduring concepts, situational application, calculations, diagnosis, and best-action reasoning.
Legacy material was treated as reference only: wording was rewritten and older/time-sensitive facts were not copied blindly.
Existing 660 question IDs and order are preserved.

questions.explanation: In the knowledge stage, the individual becomes aware of an innovation and gains initial understanding before forming an attitude.
optionExplanations: Correct. Awareness and basic understanding characterize knowledge.
Persuasion involves forming a favorable or unfavorable attitude.
Decision involves choosing to adopt or reject.
Confirmation follows implementation and seeks reinforcement.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension & Communication
questions.question: An extension worker begins a pest-management session by asking farmers to analyze problems they actually faced last season. Why is this effective for adult learners?
options: It connects new learning with prior experience and real problems
It replaces all technical evidence with anecdotes
It ensures everyone already knows the answer
questions.explanation: Adult learning is strengthened when instruction is relevant, problem-centered, and linked to learners' accumulated experience.
optionExplanations: Correct. Experience becomes a resource for learning.
The method actively encourages participation.
Experience should be integrated with, not substituted for, sound technical evidence.
The exercise diagnoses and builds understanding rather than assuming mastery.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension & Communication
questions.question: A barangay extension program is being designed for recurring vegetable losses. Which first step best reflects participatory planning?
options: Work with farmers and stakeholders to diagnose needs, constraints, and priorities
Finalize the program without consulting intended participants
Choose activities only because they were used in another province
questions.explanation: Participatory extension starts with joint situation analysis and needs assessment so objectives and interventions address locally defined problems.
optionExplanations: Correct. Joint diagnosis builds relevance and ownership.
Excluding participants undermines participation.
Copying activities without local diagnosis can misfit the situation.
Evaluation design follows clear problems and objectives.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension & Communication
questions.question: A farmer group doubts whether a recommended variety will outperform their current variety under local conditions. Which extension approach best provides convincing local evidence?
options: A result demonstration comparing the recommendation with the existing practice
A lecture unrelated to the crop
A communication channel with no field comparison
A rumor from an unknown source
questions.explanation: A result demonstration shows the outcome of a recommended practice under local conditions, helping farmers judge its relative advantage.
optionExplanations: Correct. It demonstrates what happens when the recommendation is used.
An unrelated lecture does not provide local comparative evidence.
Without a field result, the outcome is not demonstrated.
An unknown rumor lacks credibility and evidence.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension & Communication
questions.question: An extension worker wants to accelerate diffusion of a new practice without relying solely on mass media. Which local actors are especially useful to engage?

Only people with no contact with farmers
Individuals known to reject every innovation automatically
Random outsiders with no local credibility

optionExplanations: Correct. Credibility and network position make them influential.

Automatic rejection is not the desired influence path.
Local credibility matters in interpersonal diffusion.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension & Communication
questions.question: During a consultation, two vocal members dominate while women and younger farmers remain silent. What should a skilled facilitator do?
options: Acknowledge the active speakers, then deliberately invite quieter groups to contribute
Let the loudest members decide for everyone
questions.explanation: Inclusive facilitation manages participation so different stakeholders can contribute without humiliating or silencing participants.
optionExplanations: Correct. This broadens participation respectfully.
Dominance can distort the group's real priorities.
Ending the meeting avoids rather than solves the participation problem.
Shaming reduces psychological safety and participation.
